english.notes:
(i) This offence only applies in relation to domestic abuse protection orders (DAPOs) made within pilot areas, in the specified period -
(a) in the London boroughs of Bromley, Croydon and Sutton and the Metropolitan District of Greater Manchester for the period beginning with 27th November 2024, see the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 (Commencement No. 6 and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2024;
(b) in the non-metropolitan county of Cleveland for the period beginning with 5th March 2025, see the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 (Commencement No. 7 and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2025; and (c) in the non-metropolitan districts of Hartlepool, Middlesborough, Redcar and Cleveland and Stockton-on-Tees for the period beginning with 11th March 2025, see the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 (Commencement No. 8 and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2025.
The pilot ends on 26th November 2025.
(ii) For further details on the pilot see the notes on section 27 of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021.
(iii) In a case where the order was made against the person without that person being given notice of the proceedings, the person commits an offence under this section only in respect of behaviour engaged in at a time when the person was aware of the existence of the order, section 39(2) of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021, and section 45(8) and (9) where an order has been varied.
(iv) A person cannot be convicted for this offence in respect of any behaviour which has been punished as contempt of court (section 39(3)).
(v) For the power of a constable to arrest P without warrant for breach of a domestic abuse protection order (DAPO), see section 24 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 (as referred to in section section 40(9) of the 2019 Act). An additional power to enter and search premises to arrest a person who is in breach of a domestic abuse protection order is provided in section 17(1)(cza) of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984. Warrants for arrest are provided for in section 40 and Schedule 1.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
